title: Hiding the pill for an hour shows a short toast with Undo, as Wispr does
prompt: Wispr Flow parity gap G1 (docs/loop/evidence/wispr-parity-2026-11-07/SHEET.md row 13). Wispr: right-click the bar, choose Hide for 1 hour, and a notification with Undo appears for about 6 seconds, shown at most twice per user; Undo ends that snooze (wispr-help-docs-2026-11-07.txt:111-113). Yap: desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:9043 hide_for_an_hour hides the pill silently. The only way back is the tray's Show Pill Now (tray_menu.rs:537-554 PillHide) or a restart, and a user who mis-clicked the pill's right-click menu (tray_menu.rs:648) has no visible way to undo. DO: when the pill is hidden from the pill menu or the tray, show one short toast for about 6 s ('Pill hidden for an hour' + Undo) on the surface that stays visible: the main window toast (appShell.ts toast()) if it is open, otherwise a system notification through the existing notification path. Never the hidden pill itself. Undo calls the same show_pill_now path as the tray item (lib.rs TrayCommand::ShowPillNow). Show the toast at most twice ever; persist a counter in settings, and the third and later hides stay silent like Wispr. A hide while a take or meeting is live still never hides the live pill (tray_menu.rs:553-554); the toast then says the pill comes back after the take or meeting. Telemetry: one 'pill hide_toast shown=<n> undo=<bool>' log line. Code only; no cargo/npm.
acceptance: (1) a unit test that the toast is due only for the first two hides (counter persisted, third hide silent); (2) a test that Undo dispatches the same command as the tray's Show Pill Now; (3) hide during a live take or meeting keeps the pill visible and words the toast accordingly (test on the copy chooser); (4) one log line per hide carrying shown count and undo, never text; (5) INTEGRATOR: on Yap Test, hide from the pill's right-click menu and capture the toast at 2x, press Undo and see the pill return.

title: A third fn tap right after a double-tap cancels the hands-free take instead of stopping it
prompt: Wispr Flow parity gap G2 (docs/loop/evidence/wispr-parity-2026-11-07/SHEET.md rows 3-4). Wispr: double-press Fn within 500 ms starts hands-free, and 'a third press within the same 500 ms cancels a just-started hands-free session' (wispr-help-docs-2026-11-07.txt:236-237). Yap: desktop/src-tauri/src/ptt_macos.rs:916-925 (on_down, the hands_free branch) treats ANY press while hands-free as a stop: it emits HandsFreeOff + Stop, so a fumbled triple-tap sends a near-empty take through decode and shows 'empty' or pastes noise. Yap's double-tap window is DOUBLE_TAP_MS = 450 (ptt_macos.rs:703) against Wispr's 500. DO: in the PTT state machine, a press that arrives within DOUBLE_TAP_MS of the hands-free start (take_started_at, set in on_tap_up at ptt_macos.rs:986-990) emits a new PttEvent (for example HandsFreeCancel) instead of Stop. lib.rs handles it through the one cancel path (cancel_take, lib.rs:3949), so the clip is parked as Y3-D does and the pill shows the calm 'cancelled' phase, not an error. A press after the window still stops and pastes exactly as today. Do NOT change DOUBLE_TAP_MS without a measurement: add a comment naming Wispr's 500 ms and leave the value unless the ptt tests show 500 does not collide with TAP_MAX_MS/HOLD_ARM_MS. The mouse hands-free toggle (toggle_hands_free, ptt_macos.rs:1001) gets the same rule. Telemetry: 'ptt hands_free_cancel ms_since_start=<n>'. Code only; no cargo/npm.
acceptance: (1) a ptt_macos unit test: tap, tap (hands-free on), third tap 200 ms later yields the cancel event and no Stop; (2) a test: third tap 900 ms later still yields HandsFreeOff + Stop (unchanged); (3) the same two cases for the mouse hands-free toggle; (4) lib.rs routes the cancel event through cancel_take (source-scan or unit test), so the clip is parked and the pill phase is 'cancelled'; (5) one log line per cancel carrying a duration only; (6) INTEGRATOR: on Yap Test, triple-tap fn in TextEdit: nothing pastes and History shows a parked, cancelled take.

title: The pill acknowledges an fn press in its first frame (Wispr's ready state), not 280 ms later
prompt: Wispr Flow parity gap G3 (docs/loop/evidence/wispr-parity-2026-11-07/SHEET.md row 11). Wispr's bar has a 'ready' state (armed, not yet listening) between resting and listening (desktop/src/pill/dock-geometry.json:31-38 maps it, from bundle research). Yap's fn press emits no event at all until the 280 ms hold arm: ptt_macos.rs:931-942 (on_down returns only pre_arm/arm_hold), and HOLD_ARM_MS = 280 at ptt_macos.rs:701. So for the first 280 ms of every press the pill shows nothing, although capture has already started (SP-09). Yap only uses the 'ready' geometry for model-loading. STEP 1 (required, before code): on the live Wispr Flow build, capture an fn press-and-hold at 60 fps (headless capture rules apply; check the frontmost app before every key) and confirm Wispr's bar changes before listening starts. If it does not, close this item as no-gap with the capture as evidence. STEP 2: add an 'arming' pill phase driven by a new 'ptt_pressed' event emitted from on_down (no keycode, no text). The pill shows the dock-geometry 'ready' box for it, settles to listening on Start, and back to idle on a tap that becomes neither hold nor double-tap (so a double-tap shows one smooth arming→listening, never a flash to idle in between: hold the arming state for DOUBLE_TAP_MS after a short tap). It follows the approved pill artifact under ~/Obsidian/Wilson-Brain/Projects/Yap/design-2026-11-06/ (exactly one pill surface; size from the artifact, measured). Reduce Motion swaps the transition for an instant change. Telemetry: 'pill arming shown=<bool> ms_to_listening=<n>'. Code only; no cargo/npm.
acceptance: (1) the live Wispr capture from STEP 1 is saved under docs/loop/evidence/<id>/ with its verdict; (2) a ptt_macos unit test that on_down emits the pressed event exactly once per press; (3) a live.ts reducer test: pressed → arming, Start → listening, a short tap with no second tap → idle after DOUBLE_TAP_MS, double-tap → arming → listening with no idle in between; (4) pill-matrix 2x PNG of 'arming' at every dock next to the artifact crop; (5) a Reduce Motion test; (6) INTEGRATOR: on Yap Test, a 60 fps capture of fn press shows the arming state within one frame.
